newsitem.title: POLAND: WARSAW BOURSE SEEN EYEING U.S. RATES NEXT WEEK.
newsitem.headline: WARSAW BOURSE SEEN EYEING U.S. RATES NEXT WEEK.

text.p: The Warsaw bourse is seen among other exchanges holding breath ahead of Tuesday's U.S. Fed meeting with investors waiting for its outcome before deciding whether recent falls were deep enough to resume buying.
Analysts said the bourse, which has fallen 12.9 percent since its February 18 three-year high of 18,339.4, could bottom out around 15,500, possibly late next week or early in April.
Analysts said after the Fed's meeting the bourse was likely to shadow other exchanges but were split over what would be the markets' reaction.

They said Poland's growth, falling inflation, which finance minister sees possibly below 17 percent year-on-year this month, made Warsaw market a good long-term investment and the falls would sooner or later spur buying.

"Poland is always a long-term favourite for investors and it will continue to be so...but people are looking for more reasonable price levels," said Stephen Pettyfer, an analyst at Merrill Lynch in London.

They said most Warsaw stocks were fairly valued, but said recent falls made some of them such as construction stocks attractive, with Budimex trading at 12.1 times historic earnings, against 14.9 of the whole market.

"I think what we are going to see is that foreign investors are going to be looking much more closely at individual stocks rather than looking at the index as a whole," said Sonja Shechter od Daiwa in London.
The main market's WIG index fell 4.3 percent this week to 15,969.9 points on Friday.

Subscription for 1.19-million Agros shares priced at 70 zlotys per share end on Wednesday next week. The subscription of a 1.235-million share Agros's offering in large investor tranche ends later today.
Espebepe fell 46.4 percent this week on growing fears that the company would go bankrupt, after a decision of its creditors on a possible debt write-off deal was put off until April 14.
Kable , which rose 7.8 percent this week, was the main market's top gainer, after it showed better-than-expected February earnings.
